# PR Summary

<!-- Summarize your PR between here and the checklist. -->

Fixes #21116

This PR contains the code changes required for Option 2 described in linked issue.

Changed parameter type of `-PropertyType` to `RegistryValueKind`  for `New-ItemProperty` command.

## PR Context

This type change enables tab completion automatically on this parameter, instead having to create an argument completer, like in Option 1 implementation #21117.

issue_context.title: `New-ItemProperty -PropertyType` should have tab completion
issue_context.body:
### Summary of the new feature / enhancement

Currently `New-ItemProperty -PropertyType` does not have tab completion for the following registry value kinds below:

Unknown
String
ExpandString
Binary
DWord
MultiString
QWord
None

Which are documented [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.management/new-itemproperty?view=powershell-7.3#-propertytype).

Additionally, something worth noting is the type documented for this parameter is `RegistryValueKind` but the type is actually `string`, which seems like an issue in itself to fix the documentation. Can probably raise another issue for this.

### Proposed technical implementation details (optional)

#### Option 1

- Create argument completer which goes through values of `RegistryValueKind` and matches `wordToComplete` with possible enum values.
- Make sure path is using `Registry` provider and ignore any other provider.
- Add `ArgumentCompleter` attribute to `PropertyType` parameter.

#### Option 2 (Preferrable)

- Change type of `PropertyType` to `RegistryValueKind`. This will enable tab completion automatically since this type is an enum.
- Benefit here is that it aligns directly with documentation and is simpler. I don't believe this is a breaking change, since user can use enum parameter with strings the same way as before.
comments: If the parameter is dynamic and coming from Registry provider we could make it `RegistryValueKind`. In the case the completion would work automatically.

> If the parameter is dynamic and coming from Registry provider we could make it `RegistryValueKind`. In the case the completion would work automatically.

Yeah that was the other option as well. Seems like that was the intention since documentation is using `RegistryValueKind` as type. Not sure on the history if this was a mistake in implementation to use `string` or if it was deliberate. Probably need others to weigh in on that if anyone knows.
I have created two PRs with both options. If one of the options is chosen, I will make sure the other is closed.

> Not sure on the history if this was a mistake in implementation to use `string` or if it was deliberate. Probably need others to weigh in on that if anyone knows.

Perhaps there was a concern that there might be a type conflict, while string can be tried to convert to any type, but it makes no sense, because it is a dynamic parameter and even if another provider has a parameter with the same name, there is no conflict, because the path unambiguously defines the provider, and the provider unambiguously defines the type of the dynamic parameter.

Looks like Option 2 requires too many changes to public API to accommodate the type change. 

We had a couple options:

1. Change existing public API to expect `RegistryValueKind` instead of `string`. This is a breaking change. 
2. Create new public API overloads to support new type, which seems like too much work and refactoring for what it's worth. Could be done but you'd have to make a lot of changes to existing API to make this worth it and reuse implementation between overloads.
3. Convert `RegistryValueKind` to `string` using `ToString()` in cmdlet so we can use existing public API. Problem here is that there is too much converting back and forth between types: `RegistryValueKind` -> `string` -> `RegistryValueKind`. This is probably the easiest option but is very awkward.

Discussed above with @iSazonov and none of the options seem good, so opting to go with Option 1 and just use an argument completer.
@MartinGC94 Have you thoughts how we could implement a completer for the `PropertyType` parameter?

I agree with @ArmaanMcleod and think option 1 is best. As for the completer itself, feel free to take inspiration from my own here:  https://github.com/MartinGC94/UsefulArgumentCompleters/blob/main/ScriptCompleters/Shared/ItemProperty.ps1 though looking at it now, I guess I should have used the `Path` parameter instead of `LiteralPath` when the `fakeBoundParameters` contains `Path`.

> One more question. If we implement the partial completer what if an user already has custom completer and maybe for another property provider? Will we break the custom completer?

In my experience, the latest one that is applied with `Register-ArgumentCompleter` takes priority so that shouldn't be a problem.

📣 Hey @ArmaanMcleod, how did we do? We would love to hear your feedback with the link below! 🗣️ 🔗 https://aka.ms/PSRepoFeedback
Microsoft Forms

review_comments: We can not change public API, and it is an interface. So it was my wrong proposal.

In this case the only option is to use ToString() on `RegistryValueKind` in cmdlet like in a82a99b7d82c75530931404af69e7bc4da3b84f3. 

But then so much converting back and forth to get registry value. The cmdlet converts to string then the provider converts back to `RegistryValueKind` 😄.
Or we can create overloads for public api to not change existing one. I feel that option is too much work though.

> Better to close the PR.

Had a feeling it would be too hard. Oh well, at least I tried and understand internals a lot more now with registry provider.
